guard.quote: If a claim isn't in your resume, you find out before the recruiter does.
guard.body: The guard rebuilds a facts ledger from the tailored résumé and diffs it against the one built from your original. Employers, titles, dates, credentials and numbers that appeared from nowhere are flagged one by one, and you see them before you download anything.

score.quote: The match score can show its work, term by term.
score.body: Keyword coverage is plain deterministic Python: which terms the job asked for, which ones your résumé already earned, and which ones the rewrite surfaced. Only the recruiter-fit half of the score ever asks a model.
score.source: The scorer — measured before and after every tailor

ats.quote: Eleven format checks, and not one of them needs an API key.
ats.body: Date formats, acronym pairing, pronouns, bullet length, résumé length weighed against your actual years of experience. Because it's deterministic it's instant, free, and identical every time you run it.

faq.title: Straight answers
faq.q1: Does JobFinder make things up on my resume?
faq.a1: No — and that's the whole point. A code-enforced Fabrication Guard diffs every tailored claim against a ledger built from your original resume. Anything it can't trace back to your real experience is flagged, per claim, before you download. Skills are the one deliberate exception: adopting the job's wording for something you genuinely do is honest tailoring, not fabrication.
faq.q2: Will the output pass ATS screening?
faq.a2: Both exporters enforce ATS-safe rules by construction: single column, standard section names, no tables, text boxes, images, headers or footers — just clean, selectable text. The release suite renders every template in both formats and both languages and re-extracts the text to prove it stays parseable. No tool can promise a specific company's screener will like you, but nothing in the file is there to trip one.
faq.q3: Do I need an account or a subscription?
faq.a3: There are no accounts, no email and no billing anywhere in the product. The hosted build is gated by a single access code stored on your device — that's a door key, not a profile. The free CV scan is outside the gate entirely. It also runs fully offline with a built-in stub, so you can exercise the whole pipeline without an API key.
faq.q4: How is this different from auto-apply tools?
faq.a4: Auto-apply tools optimize for volume and often submit generic, fabricated applications that get flagged. JobFinder optimizes for quality and truth: you stay in control of what's sent, and every claim is defensible. Automated submission exists for exactly one board, only for kits you approved and the guard cleared — LinkedIn is never automated.
faq.q5: Can I choose how the resume looks?
faq.a5: Yes. Each template is its own palette, type hierarchy and vertical rhythm, and you switch at download time without re-running the tailor. They share one design system, so the DOCX and the PDF read as the same document rather than two cousins.
faq.a6: End to end: the interface, the parsing, the tailoring and both exports. The PDF has its own layout engine that line-breaks and bidi-reorders line by line instead of leaning on a direction-blind paragraph engine, and the Hebrew DOCX mirrors weight and size onto the complex-script properties Word actually reads. Mixed Hebrew/English résumés work too.
